investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the pending state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it, and the other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector rules. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the production-api Kubernetes cluster's peer-pod VM resource pool; it is an eval-detected signal, not a confirmed user-traffic incident.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three sibling check failures (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the pod's affinity/selector rules restrict scheduling to only the 2 kata-capable nodes, so even if other nodes had spare CPU/memory, they cannot accept the pod. The '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' clause in the scheduler message (failed-check.message) confirms this constraint is active.

Tertiary — peer-pod VM quota or limit set too low for the cluster: the cluster may have a hard limit on the number of concurrent kata peer-pod VMs that is lower than current demand, causing the resource to appear exhausted even if underlying hypervisor capacity exists.

Lower confidence — transient spike in concurrent remote agent workloads consuming all VM slots at the time of the eval run: if other jobs or users were holding VM slots, the pool could have been temporarily full rather than permanently exhausted.

The snapshot was last published approximately 338 minutes prior, meaning the workflow either did not trigger on schedule, failed silently, or its published artifact was not updated despite a run. investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the pending state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it, and the other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector rules. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the production-api Kubernetes cluster's peer-pod VM resource pool; it is an eval-detected signal, not a confirmed user-traffic incident.
